name: Dentecs
summary: Four workspaces for a dental clinic on one data model, built around the FDI tooth-numbering standard, with prices frozen onto every treatment session.
oneLiner: Clinic software that thinks in teeth.
role: Data model, API and role workspaces

overview.what: A dental clinic management system with four workspaces over one shared data model: reception, treatment, accounting and management. It includes an interactive dental chart, multi-tooth treatment sessions, orthodontic planning, prescriptions, X-ray storage and invoicing.
overview.who: Dental clinic staff. Reception books and registers, doctors treat and record, accounting invoices, and management configures the price list and watches the numbers.
overview.problem: A clinic is four jobs that barely overlap, and generic practice software crowds them onto one screen. It also has to be precise: a system that records “tooth 7” will eventually put a filling on the wrong side of someone's mouth.

roleDetail.summary: My first professional project. I met the dentist to gather requirements, then built the data model, the API and the four workspaces.
items: 19 models and 57 API endpoints in Django REST Framework
The interactive dental chart, multi-tooth sessions and orthodontic planning
An appointment scheduler, invoicing, and a full-screen waiting-room display
Speech-to-text for clinical notes and QR-code patient lookup
Started with server-rendered templates, then split the system into a REST API and a React frontend after a senior engineer's review

architecture.caption: The data model knows it is about teeth.

components.title: Patient
components.body: Carries per-tooth JSON maps keyed by FDI code: whether each tooth is present, orthodontic anchor points, and the links between anchored teeth.

components.title: Treatment session
components.body: One visit, one doctor, many teeth and many procedures, with the price of each procedure copied onto the session.

components.title: Clinic records
components.body: Appointments, invoices with serial numbers, prescriptions, diagnoses, treatment plans, panoramic X-rays and lab orders.

components.title: Four workspaces
components.body: Reception, treatment, accounting and management as separate React areas over one Django REST API.

implementation.title: Domain model
implementation.body: FDI notation throughout: 32 permanent and 20 primary teeth addressed by quadrant and position, in the models, the seed fixtures and the frontend chart.

implementation.title: Orthodontics
implementation.body: Anchor connections between teeth are stored per patient as a graph and drawn as lines on the chart.

implementation.title: Work classification
implementation.body: Each procedure type has a colour and an icon that render directly on the chart, so a doctor reads a patient's history as marks across the mouth instead of rows in a table.

implementation.title: Interface
implementation.body: A scheduler built on FullCalendar and DHTMLX, printable invoices, an ApexCharts dashboard, QR generation and scanning, and speech recognition for notes.

implementation.title: Stack
implementation.body: Django 4.1, Django REST Framework and MySQL. React 18 with Redux Toolkit, MUI and Ant Design on the Mantis admin template, with an Arabic translation layer through i18next.

decisions.title: Speak the dentist's standard
decisions.context: Teeth aren't a list of 32 things. Dentists address them by quadrant and position.
decisions.decision: Adopt FDI World Dental Federation notation everywhere, and initialise each patient's per-tooth maps on first save.
decisions.tradeoff: More domain research before the first model, and a schema a dentist would recognise.

decisions.title: Freeze prices onto the session
decisions.context: Raising the price of a crown next month must not change last month's invoice.
decisions.decision: Copy each procedure's price onto the treatment session when it is recorded.
decisions.tradeoff: A little duplicated data, and invoices that never drift. The same rule later reappeared in the Geofence payroll.
decisions.code:
# this field holds the works prices, so that changing the work price
# won't affect the session
works_prices = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True, null=True)

decisions.title: Dictation for gloved hands
decisions.context: A dentist in the middle of a treatment can't type.
decisions.decision: Speech recognition for clinical notes in the treatment screens.
decisions.tradeoff: A browser feature with uneven support, used where it removes the most friction.

challenges.problem: Invoicing a visit that covers several teeth as one unit.
challenges.solution: A multi-tooth session model: one visit, many teeth, many procedures, one payment state.

challenges.problem: Reading a long treatment history at a glance.
challenges.solution: Colour-and-icon classifications drawn on the chart per tooth.

challenges.problem: The first version mixed server-rendered pages with business logic.
challenges.solution: Rebuilt as a Django REST API with a separate React frontend, which I learned for the purpose.

results.status: Delivered as a private deployment for a dental clinic. There is no public instance; screenshots use seeded demo patients.
notes: The UI shell is based on the Mantis MUI template; all clinic functionality is built on top of it.
